label: input c at original positions 1-5
explanation: Token-and-position feature: fires only when the input token is the letter c during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at positions 1-5. It never fires on any other token, never at position 0 or at positions 6+, and never at the delimiter or in the copy phase (not even when c is fed back as input or is being output). Magnitude depends on position: strongest at t=2-4 (top activations at t=3, about 74% of mass at t=2-3), weak at t=1 (~5% of mass) and t=5 (~2% of mass, many inactive). The false positives (~11%) are mostly c at t=1 or t=5 that stay inactive. A repeated c (not the first occurrence) is slightly less likely to fire, but excluding repeats lowers F1. Previous tokens, first token, and L have little effect.

issues: All the main claims hold up. On the test split the predicate scores P 0.887, R 1.0, F1 0.940 and mass recall 1.0, with 0 missed activations. The dev profile shows activity only on in_tok=c in the original phase at t=1..5. Activity is zero at t=0, at t>=6, at the delimiter and in the copy phase.
The magnitude claims match the dev profile. Mass share is 0.049 at t=1, 0.363 at t=2, 0.375 at t=3, 0.196 at t=4 and 0.017 at t=5, so t=2 and t=3 together hold about 74%.

The false positives (8427 test steps) all sit at t=1 (precision 0.87) and t=5 (precision 0.44). I found no length structure in them. At t=5, precision is 0.42 for L=6 and 0.45 for L>6. At t=1, precision is 0.87 for L<=5 and 0.87 for L>5. Excluding the last original token (to_go>0) lowered F1 to 0.896.
The narrower predicate t=2..4 reproduces on test: P 1.0, R 0.708.

Minor: I could not reproduce the claim about repeated c. Adding n_seen(['c'])==0 gave exactly the same scores as the base predicate, and n_seen(['c'])>0 gave 0. Either the helper does not behave as expected here or repeats are never predicted. This is a side remark in the explanation, not part of the label or predicate.
The label 'input c at original positions 1-5' matches the predicate and does not overclaim.
